Principle 18: Korean Holidays
An Introduction to Korean Holidays
Holidays are a special time when families in Korea can get together and celebrate.
My country has many traditional holidays.
Like many Asian countries, we celebrate New Year’s Day, Independence Day, Arbor Day, Buddha’s Birthday and many more.
I would like to tell you about the two largest traditional holidays in Korea: Lunar New Year’s and Chu-Seok.
Lunar New Year's Day
The first big holiday is Lunar New Year’s , which is also known as Seo--Lal.
It is celebrated on the first day of the first month on the lunar calendar, which is usually after the 1st of January on the solar calendar.
The most important Lunar New Year custom is the ancestral memorial ceremony.
가장 중요한 설날의 관습은 조상의 기념 의식이다.
가족 구성원 각자는 아침 일찍 일어나 그들의 가장 좋은 옷을 입는다.
그 후에, 우리의 조상들에게 경의를 표하는 의식을 행한다.
이 의식 다음으로, 어린 사람들이 그들의 윗사람들에게 모두 다가오는 새해동안 많은 축복이 있기를 기원하며 절을 한다.
Chu-Seok
Chu-seok is the biggest national holiday of the year, and it is often referred to as the Korean Thanksgiving.
During Chu-seok, people visit their ancestrial tombs and make an offering of food to their ancestors.
In addition, most people play games with their relatives and make song-pyeun, which is a Korean traditional rice cake.
I like our country’s traditional holidays.
On these days I learn how important family is!
